Time Series 5: State-Space Models¶

A state-space model describes an observed series as the noisy view of a hidden state that evolves in time. Trends, seasonal patterns, regressions with time-varying coefficients and ARMA models are all of this form, and one algorithm, the Kalman filter, handles every one of them: it updates the state estimate observation by observation, copes with missing values, and gives the exact Gaussian log-likelihood. After this chapter you can write a model in state-space form, filter and smooth a series, forecast with uncertainty, choose unknown noise levels by likelihood, and simulate.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program.

The model¶

x_{t+1} = A x_t + B w_t, y_t = C x_t + D v_t,

with w_t and v_t independent standard normal vectors. SsmModel holds the matrices and the distribution of the state before the first observation:

Field

Shape

Meaning

transition

m × m

A, how the state evolves

state_loading

m × k

B, how the state shocks enter

observation

n × m

C, how the state shows in the observation

innovation_loading

n × h

D, observation noise

mean0, cov0

m, m × m

mean and covariance of the state before the first observation

Because the initial moments describe the state one step before the first observation, the first forecast of the state is A mean0 with covariance A cov0 A' + B B'. A large cov0 expresses ignorance about the starting level. Only the matrices appear: noise standard deviations go in B and D, so the noise covariances are B B' and D D'.

All functions are static members of Ssm:

Function

Result

filter(y, model)

SsmFilterResult: filtered_states [T, m], filtered_states_cov [T, m, m], forecasted_states and forecasted_states_cov (the prediction for time t made at t − 1), forecasted_obs, forecasted_obs_cov, forecast_obs_error, kalman_gain [T, m, n], data_used [T, n], loglik_per_obs [T] and loglik

smooth(y, model)

SsmSmoothResult: the filter result plus smoothed_states and smoothed_states_cov

forecast(h, y, model)

SsmForecastResult: observations, observations_cov, states, states_cov for the h steps after the data

forecast(h, model)

the same from the initial state alone

simulate(T, model, num_paths, cfg, seed)

SsmSimResult: observations, states, state_disturbance, obs_innovation (with a leading path dimension when num_paths > 1)

Here y is a T × n matrix. Missing observations are NaN: the update is skipped there (data_used is 0) and the uncertainty widens until data return. SsmOptions::tolerance (default 0) makes the filter ignore an observation channel whose forecast variance is at or below that value, which guards against channels carrying no information.

The log-likelihood is the exact one for the model and the supplied noise levels. The library does not search over noise levels for you; evaluating loglik over a grid, or passing it to any of the optimisers of the numerical chapters, estimates them by maximum likelihood.

Programs¶

  • Filtering a local linear trend

  • Smoothing across a gap, and forecasting

  • Simulation as a check

Checklist¶

  1. Write the model as x_{t+1} = A x_t + B w_t, y_t = C x_t + D v_t and enter standard deviations (not variances) in B and D.

  2. Give the initial state a wide cov0 when you do not know the starting level.

  3. Mark missing observations with NaN rather than dropping them, so the time index stays intact.

  4. Choose unknown noise levels by maximising loglik; check the result with smooth and simulate.

  5. Use filtered states for real-time decisions and smoothed states for looking back.
